name: mpd_pdm_100um
label: MPD PDM 100 um silicon SPAD, free-beam (NIM timing, 50 ps)
sources: PicoQuant / Micro Photon Devices PDM series datasheet (February 2018, 25 C): spectral range ~400-1000 nm peaking near 550 nm; PDE typical 24 % at 400, 49 % at 550, 37 % at 650 nm (free-beam; the FC/PC fibre version loses up to 20 % absolute); 100 um active diameter; TTL output 250 ps FWHM, NIM timing output ~50 ps FWHM (worse towards the blue); dead time 77 ns typical (7-8 % loss at 1 Mcps, ~25 % at 4 Mcps); afterpulsing <= 3 % (0.13 % typical per Laser 2000); dark-count grades for 100 um < 500 / 250 / 100 / 50 / 25 cps; gating input; 5-12 V
ASU intensity-interferometry group: factory jitter 32 ps on their 100 um units, 40 % PDE at 589 nm through the FC connector, 50 cps dark counts
P. Nugent, 2026-10-21: the ISI detector, free-beam module at prime focus (100 um = ~4 arcsec)
notes: The free-beam module at the ISI prime focus: no fibre, so no coupling loss and no modal dispersion; the 100 um active area is ~4 arcsec, so the telescope throughput carries no slit loss.

PDE: the datasheet's three points (400, 550, 650 nm); the rest of the curve (peak shape, 0.20 at 800, 0.11 at 900, 0.03 at 1000 nm) is an ASSUMED silicon-SPAD shape -- the 900 nm filter depends on it; nothing beyond 1000 nm.

Timing 50 ps FWHM is the datasheet's NIM figure demonstrated on 50 um devices; the ASU 100 um units measured 32 ps; larger SPADs may carry a longer diffusion tail, so the measured IRF of the actual unit at 900 nm is wanted.
Dark 50 cps: the grade ASU received (grades down to < 25 cps exist).

max_total_cps 4e6 is an OPERATING CAP (not a device limit): the user's 'stay at a few Mcps per channel'; dead-time load r tau = 0.31 there (25 % loss), the non-paralyzable model is applied and stays trustworthy. The runners attenuate brighter stars to it as a neutral-density filter would.
assumptions: pde_table_nm between and beyond the three datasheet points (900 nm in particular)
